facts.condition: If the two receiver profiles are uniformly perturbed, each constraint in the fixed converse system admits an explicit linear error allowance, with each receiver's coefficient no larger than four.

Whenever a converse witness has positive margin in every constraint, sufficiently accurate finite-support receiver approximations retain feasibility after applying the rowwise error allowances; this implication does not cover boundary-optimal witnesses or continuity of the unmodified optimum.

For binary-input receivers represented by fair-prior posterior laws, a channel-independent continuity modulus makes the resulting information profiles precompact in the uniform topology; refining symmetric grids yield bounded-support representatives converging uniformly.

assumptions: No conclusion is assumed about exact capacity, receiver optimality, minimax exchange, or attainment of the unmodified optimization problem.
Receiver comparison uses the uniform norm on complete prior-indexed information profiles.
The finite grids include both endpoints and the fair-prior midpoint and are closed under reflection.
The previously accepted converse-system construction and finite-grid posterior representation remain available as dependencies.
